one_liner: Senior FinCEN regulatory writer who drafts and reviews Bank Secrecy Act anti-money-laundering regulations and guidance, working closely with Treasury lawyers.
fit_summary: This GS-13/14 role requires a year of GS-12/13-level experience analyzing or writing anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing or financial-crimes regulations. Daniel's policy work is research on the Rural Health Transformation Program and on a state health agency's training recertification, not financial regulation, so he is unlikely to be rated qualified.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens or nationals) under Direct-Hire authority; no federal status needed and veterans' preference does not apply.

GS-13: one year of specialized experience at GS-12 level analyzing statutes/regulations or reviewing, interpreting or writing regulations or guidance related to AML, CFT, financial crimes, or similar laws.
GS-14: the GS-13 experience plus coordinating and implementing AML/CFT/financial-crimes programs, policies and operations, at GS-13 level.
No degree required, but you must pass a Moderate Risk Public Trust Tier 2 background investigation, Continuous Vetting, FBI Rap Back and an ethics/financial-interest review.
Applicants must complete the questionnaire and the USA Hire online assessment by the cut date they apply under.
strategy: Skip this one: his FEMA Public Assistance onboarding and county grant work don't amount to a year of analyzing financial-crimes or similar regulations.

Put the effort into better-fit roles in FEMA, Virginia VDEM or Northern Virginia county emergency management, where his background fits directly, or in legislative offices that suit his interest in policy.
resume_bullets: Studied economic globalization, global trade relations and foreign investment for an M.A. in Global Affairs (George Mason, 2016).
Provided scholarly research that helped a state public health agency's analysts review trauma-incident training recertification.
interview_questions: Walk us through a time you interpreted a complex statute or regulation and turned it into practical guidance.
How would you balance regulatory burden on financial institutions against law-enforcement needs when drafting a BSA rule?
Describe how you worked with attorneys or reviewers to get a document cleared and resolved disagreements.
Tell us about a time you influenced stakeholders who initially opposed a policy recommendation.
watch_outs: The AML/CFT/financial-crimes specialized experience requirement is the main barrier; emergency-management experience will likely not count unless it clearly involved analyzing comparable regulations.
Tier 2 Public Trust investigation, Continuous Vetting and the financial conflict-of-interest review are conditions of employment.
The job is in DC and is not remote, so expect a commute from Manassas on office days despite telework eligibility.
